title: A first collaboration conversation: CBL-related disorder and CTF

sentences.text: On behalf of RASopathies Network, we would welcome a conversation with Children's Tumor Foundation (CTF) about including CBL families in shared research efforts.
CBL-related disorder and NF1 share loss of function: proteins that help switch off cell signals do not work properly.
This offers a reason to explore collaboration, not proof that the same registry design will meet both communities' needs.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: Our contact registry is described as being built; its inclusion of CBL families is inferred by the atlas, rather than explicitly confirmed on its page.
The Clinical, Genetic, and Epidemiologic Study of Children and Adults With RASopathies explicitly lists CBL.
CTF's NF Registry on the IAMRARE platform includes NF1; adapting it for CBL is a possibility to explore, not an established capability.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: We should confirm whether juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia and chylothorax also occur in NF1, rather than treating missing records as evidence of absence.
The NF1 resource comparisons flag those symptoms and ten other CBL features as unrecorded; the disease comparison also names finger joint hypermobility.
We should review differences in recorded cell-signalling mechanisms—MAPK cascade and Ras protein signal transduction—listed only on the NF1 side of these resource comparisons.

If PATRAS is considered later, check missing finger joint hypermobility, deep philtrum and eight other features, plus mechanisms involving overactive proteins or altered proteins blocking normal ones and one unnamed mechanism; its PTPN11 coverage is atlas-inferred.
Send CTF one focused enquiry asking whether the NF Registry could include CBL-related disorder and what changes would need review.
No open questions are recorded yet in the supplied atlas input.
We would welcome an exploratory conversation about CBL families.
CBL-related disorder and NF1 share a loss-of-function mechanism.
Could your NF Registry potentially include CBL-related disorder?
We would like to review differences together before proposing any shared approach.
[Your name], on behalf of RASopathies Network (RASopathiesNet USA / UK)
